chains.title: Null: no TF-mediated effect of this variant
predictions: The variant will not produce a reproducible, variant-dependent TF-binding and regulatory effect in a relevant breast-cell context.
Any future disease association could reflect linkage to another causal variant or a mechanism not mediated by TF binding at this base.
falsified_if: Editing the variant produces a reproducible allele-dependent TF-binding difference and a matching TF-dependent regulatory effect in a relevant breast-cell context.

chains.title: SPDEF-mediated binding change at a regulatory site; downstream target and effect remain uncertain
chains.element: The variant lies in a VEP-annotated enhancer feature, but its connection to an active regulatory element is unresolved: no ENCODE cCRE overlaps it, and the nearest dELS is 38 bp away.

links.claim: SPDEF is the clearest factor-specific binding candidate among the supported alternatives: it is expressed and has an MCF-7 ChIP peak over the variant, and its own QBiC-SELEX model predicts stronger binding to ref G than alt A at a strong site. This predicts binding, not regulatory activity.
VEP annotates a regulatory enhancer feature at the site, but ENCODE reports no cCRE overlap; the nearby active dELS is not shown to be the same element.

TOX3 is a candidate target because it is the nearest listed protein-coding gene by TSS and has gene-level breast-cancer evidence, but no supplied evidence connects this variant or the nearby dELS to TOX3 regulation.
SPDEF is expressed in MCF-7 and has a ChIP-seq peak over the variant in that biosample.

A regulatory effect on TOX3 could be relevant to breast cancer based on gene-level evidence, but no supplied evidence links this variant or this proposed mechanism to the disease; no significant breast-tissue eQTL is reported.

predictions: An allele-specific SPDEF binding assay at the variant should favor G over A.
If this chain is correct, a variant-dependent regulatory effect should depend on SPDEF; its direction on element activity or gene expression is not established by the binding evidence.
falsified_if: A suitably controlled allele-specific assay finds no G-over-A SPDEF binding difference.
A reproducible variant-dependent regulatory effect is found but is unchanged by SPDEF perturbation.

chains.title: Possible TCF7L2-mediated gain of binding to alt A
chains.element: The variant has a VEP enhancer annotation, but its relationship to an active regulatory element is unresolved.

links.claim: TCF7L2 has an MCF-7 ChIP peak over the variant. QBiC-SELEX predicts stronger binding to alt A at a strong site, but the result uses a TCF7L1-mapped model rather than a TCF7L2-specific model, so the factor-specific inference is uncertain.

VEP annotates a regulatory enhancer feature at the site, but ENCODE reports no cCRE overlap and the nearest active dELS is 38 bp away; the evidence does not establish that these annotations identify the same element.
TOX3 is a nearby, breast-cancer-relevant candidate target, but the evidence does not show that this variant regulates TOX3.
TCF7L2 occupancy is reported over the variant in MCF-7, although its measured expression in this context is low.

A TCF7L2-dependent regulatory effect could be relevant if it alters a breast-cancer-related target, but the supplied evidence does not connect this variant or mechanism to breast cancer; no significant breast-tissue eQTL is reported.

predictions: An allele-specific TCF7L2 binding assay should favor A over G, though the prediction is based on a related-factor model.
If this chain is correct, a variant-dependent regulatory effect should be more sensitive to TCF7L2 perturbation than to SPDEF perturbation; the direction of expression change is unknown.
falsified_if: A suitably controlled allele-specific assay finds no A-over-G TCF7L2 binding difference.
A reproducible variant-dependent regulatory effect is found but is unchanged by TCF7L2 perturbation.

QBiC-SELEX screen of chr16:52565398:G>A, one line per TF, each with the TF's own or CIS-BP-mapped model of largest |z|. Candidates are TFs whose ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant and that are expressed (DepMap line ACH-000019), bound here before bound elsewhere, then a strong site before a weak one, then by |z|; then expressed TFs ENCODE never assayed whose best model passes the gate (occupancy unknown). Shown: 10 of 79 occupied (16 with a strong site), 5 of 137 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 49 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 425 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here; 20 bound but below 1 TPM. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only. Site strength is the better allele's best k-mer over the variant, as a percentile of the best model's k-mers; a strong site reaches the 97.5th. At a weak site the ChIP peak more likely reflects another site in the element.
